dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Sept 9: SPCX Falls 4% as Day-90 Lockup Unlocks 319M Shares; Starship Flight 14 Vehicles in Final Checkout
heroSubtitle: 8,892 days since SpaceX founding — SPCX shares fell more than 4% on Sept 9, from $153.47 to around $148.32, as roughly 319 million previously restricted shares (about $49B at the prior close) became eligible to trade under the Day-90 tranche of SpaceX's post-IPO lockup schedule, closely mirroring the market's reaction to the similarly sized Aug 20 unlock. A further ~59.1M affiliate shares unlock Sept 10, with a much larger ~328M-share tranche tied to November earnings. On the hardware side, Starship Flight 14's Booster 21 and Ship 41 finished their required single-vehicle tests as of Sept 7 and moved into final checkout in Starbase's Mega Bays; next up is loading the Starlink V3 payload into Ship 41 before rollout and stacking, with the Sept 15 no-earlier-than date still an unofficial planning-slide target for SpaceX's first attempt at a full orbital insertion. That follows a Sept 3-4 FAA Finding of No Significant Impact clearing added Pacific Ocean contingency splashdown zones for Ship 41. On the launch side, SpaceX flew the Starlink 15-24 mission from Vandenberg on Sept 6 (B1088, 19th flight, 27 satellites) — the year's 80th Starlink mission and 103rd Falcon 9 launch of 2026 — following the Sept 2 Starlink 15-23 flight (B1063, 35th flight).
